newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier, de Havilland union reach deal.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier, de Havilland union reach deal.

text.p: A tentative labor contract has been reached between Bombardier Inc's de Havilland unit and its unionized workers, narrowly averting a strike, the union said on Monday.

The new three-year deal was reached just minutes before the 1000 EDT/1400 GMT strike deadline set by the Canadian Auto Workers union, which represents 3,800 of the 6,326 workers at Toronto-based de Havilland aircraft maker.
CAW spokeswoman Jane Armstrong said the details of the deal will be made public later this morning.
The tentative agreement is set to be ratified by union members on Saturday.
The Downsview plant makes the de Havilland Dash-8 family of turboprop regional aircraft and is responsible for the final assembly of the new Bombardier Global Express long-range business jet.
Montreal-based Bombardier acquired control of the company from Boeing Co in 1994.
